canonical_name: SQuAD v1.1 (Stanford Question Answering Dataset; paper: 'SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text')
metric: F1 (bag-of-tokens overlap, max over gold answers) and Exact Match (EM); F1 is the headline metric
n_items_test: Hidden test: ~10% of 536 articles (46 articles); exact question count not stated in paper (implied 107,785 - 87,599 train - 10,570 dev = 9,616; unverified). De-facto standard for papers is the public dev set: 10,570 questions / 48 articles (train 87,599 / 442 articles)
n_items_source: Paper v1: 107,785 QA pairs on 536 articles, random 80/10/10 article split; dev/train counts computed from official dev-v1.1.json and train-v1.1.json (github.com/rajpurkar/SQuAD-explorer)
score_at_release_system: Logistic regression with hand-engineered features (authors' baseline)
score_at_release_setting: Supervised, trained on SQuAD train; hidden test F1 51.0 / EM 40.4 (dev F1 51.0 / EM 40.0); sliding-window baseline ~20% F1. No external leaderboard entries at launch (first: Match-LSTM, Aug 27 2016, 70.695 F1)
n_annotators: 1 held-out crowdworker answer per question (the 2nd answer) scored against the remaining answers; dev/test have 2 additional answers per question (>=3 total)
human_source: arXiv 1606.05250v1 Table 5 (test F1 86.8 / EM 77.0; dev F1 90.5 / EM 80.3). Official v1.1 leaderboard lists Human Performance F1 91.221 / EM 82.304 (re-estimate on v1.1 test; SQuAD 2.0 paper arXiv 1806.03822 cites 82.3 EM / 91.2 F1 and says the v1 single-human estimate 'likely underestimate[s] human accuracy')
test_access_notes: Test set never released; models are submitted via CodaLab Worksheets and run by organizers; train and dev public (CC BY-SA 4.0)
curation_notes: Crowdworkers (Daemo platform on Amazon Mechanical Turk; US/Canada, >=97% approval, >=1000 HITs; $9/hr) asked and answered up to 5 questions per paragraph (~4 min/paragraph) on paragraphs from 536 articles sampled uniformly from the top-10,000 English Wikipedia articles (Project Nayuki PageRank); answers are text spans
maintainer: Stanford NLP Group (Rajpurkar, Zhang, Lopyrev, Liang)
lineage: v1.0 released with paper (2016-06); v1.1 revision is what the official leaderboard and public dev JSON use; successor SQuAD 2.0 (2018-06, adds 50k+ adversarial unanswerable questions); derivatives include Adversarial SQuAD (Jia & Liang 2017-07), QNLI task in GLUE (2018-04), XQuAD (translation of v1.1 dev, 2019)
known_contamination_or_defects: Adversarial distractor sentences cut 16 published models' average F1 from 75% to 36% (Jia & Liang 2017, https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.07328); creators note the v1 human score (single human) underestimates human accuracy (https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.03822). Source passages are Wikipedia, which is in nearly all LLM pretraining corpora
notes: Release-time numbers are from the v1.0 paper; the leaderboard reports v1.1 test scores. Exact hidden-test size not published in primary sources.

canonical_name: AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) - Challenge Set ('Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge')
metric: accuracy (1 point if correct; 1/k credit for a k-way tie that includes the correct answer)
n_items_test: 1,172 (Challenge test); Challenge dev 299; Challenge train 1,119 (Challenge total 2,590). Companion Easy set: 2,251/570/2,376 (5,197)
n_items_source: arXiv 1803.05457v1 dataset split table
score_at_release_system: DGEM (AI2 decomposed graph entailment model, with ARC Corpus retrieval)
score_at_release_setting: Challenge test; supervised baselines; random guess-all = 25.02; authors state no baseline is significantly above random (95% CI +/-2.5%). Others: TableILP 26.97, BiDAF 26.54, DGEM-OpenIE 26.41, DecompAttn 24.34, TupleInference 23.83, IR (ARC Corpus) 20.26
human_source: No human baseline reported in paper v1
test_access_notes: Test questions and answer keys are distributed with the dataset; AI2 leaderboard accepts prediction submissions but labels are not hidden
curation_notes: 7,787 natural-science multiple-choice questions from standardized tests (grades 3-9; e.g., state exams, NAEP, TIMSS, plus an anonymous partner). Challenge Set = questions answered incorrectly by both an IR (retrieval) solver and a PMI word co-occurrence solver; ships with 14M-sentence ARC Corpus
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI (AI2), Aristo project
lineage: Released together with ARC-Easy and the ARC Corpus (2018-03); later ARC-DA direct-answer variant (AI2, 2021). Unrelated to Chollet's ARC-AGI
known_contamination_or_defects: Scores are highly sensitive to evaluation format (scoring options separately vs. showing all options together); Borchmann 2024 argues the 'Challenge' difficulty is largely an artifact of the separate-option setup (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17758). Questions/answers public since 2018, so web contamination is plausible
notes: Challenge set defined adversarially against two simple solvers (IR and PMI score ~1-2% on it by construction).

canonical_name: GLUE: General Language Understanding Evaluation benchmark
metric: GLUE score = macro-average over 9 tasks of task metrics (Matthews corr for CoLA; acc/F1 avg for MRPC & QQP; Pearson/Spearman avg for STS-B; accuracy elsewhere, MNLI matched/mismatched)
n_items_test: ~431k test examples across 9 tasks (v1 Table 1: CoLA 1.1k, SST-2 1.8k, MRPC 1.7k, STS-B 1.4k, QQP 391k, MNLI 20k, QNLI 11k, RTE 3k, WNLI 146) + diagnostic set of 550 sentence pairs (1,100 entailment examples)
n_items_source: arXiv 1804.07461v1 Table 1 and Section 4 (diagnostic)
score_at_release_system: Single-task BiLSTM + ELMo baseline (authors')
score_at_release_setting: Test set via evaluation server; v1 Table 5 'Avg' column. Caveat: v1 'Avg' values are lower than the simple mean of the per-task scores printed in the same rows (this row's 9 task scores average 67.0), cause not stated. Revised baselines in later arXiv versions/ICLR 2019: best = multi-task BiLSTM+Attn+ELMo 70.0, which the creators later cite as the GLUE score 'at launch' (Nangia & Bowman 2019)
score_at_release_source: arXiv 1804.07461v1 Table 5 (raw table text); arXiv 1804.07461v3 Table 4; https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10425
n_annotators: 5 crowdworkers per example (Hybrid platform), majority vote (STS-B: mean); ~500 sampled test examples per task (145 for WNLI); annotators trained on 20 dev examples, <65% disqualified
human_source: Not in paper v1 (none at release). Added by GLUE creators in 'Human vs. Muppet: A Conservative Estimate of Human Performance on the GLUE Benchmark' (Nangia & Bowman, 2019-05-24, https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10425): 87.1 overall (per-task 66.4 CoLA to 97.8 SST-2); now shown on leaderboard
test_access_notes: Test labels privately held; online evaluation platform/leaderboard at gluebenchmark.com
curation_notes: Aggregates 9 existing datasets (CoLA, SST-2, MRPC, QQP, STS-B, MNLI, QNLI recast from SQuAD, RTE, WNLI recast from Winograd) plus a new expert-curated diagnostic set
maintainer: NYU (Wang, Singh, Bowman), University of Washington (Michael, Levy), DeepMind (Hill)
lineage: Parents: the 9 constituent datasets (2005-2018) and SentEval-style evaluation; successor: SuperGLUE (2019-05); many language-specific clones (e.g., CLUE, Russian SuperGLUE)
known_contamination_or_defects: WNLI dev set is adversarial due to a data quirk (shared hypotheses between train and dev; v3 paper); NLI components have annotation artifacts (hypothesis-only cues, Gururangan et al. 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.02324)
notes: Format = sentence/sentence-pair classification and regression. Score at release depends on paper version: v1 60.3 vs revised 70.0 (cited by creators as 'at launch'); v1 averaging appears inconsistent with its per-task numbers.

canonical_name: SQuAD 2.0 ('Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD')
metric: F1 and Exact Match (EM), with abstention ('no answer') required for unanswerable questions; F1 headline
n_items_test: 8,862 (hidden test; 4,332 unanswerable; 28 articles). Public dev (de-facto for papers): 11,873 (5,945 unanswerable; 35 articles). Train 130,319 (43,498 unanswerable)
n_items_source: arXiv 1806.03822v1 dataset statistics table; dev count confirmed from official dev-v2.0.json
score_at_release_system: DocQA + ELMo (Clark & Gardner BiDAF + self-attention + ELMo, retrained by Stanford)
score_at_release_setting: Hidden test, F1 66.3 / EM 63.4 (dev 67.6 / 65.1). Leaderboard launch entries were only the 3 Stanford-run baselines dated 2018-05-30 (BiDAF+SA+ELMo 63.372 EM / 66.251 F1); first external entries late June 2018
n_annotators: Additional crowdworkers answered all dev/test questions; avg 4.8 answers per question; final answer by majority vote
human_source: arXiv 1806.03822v1 (test F1 89.5 / EM 86.9; dev 89.0 / 86.3); leaderboard Human Performance 89.452 F1 / 86.831 EM
test_access_notes: Test set not released; official evaluation by submitting models to CodaLab
curation_notes: Answerable questions reused from SQuAD 1.1; 53,775 new unanswerable questions written adversarially by Daemo crowdworkers (up to 5 per paragraph, 7 min/paragraph, $10.50/hr) to look similar to answerable ones, each with a plausible (distractor) answer span
maintainer: Stanford NLP Group (Rajpurkar, Jia, Liang)
lineage: Parent: SQuAD 1.1 (2016); SQuAD 2.0 replaced 1.1 as the primary leaderboard benchmark
known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed; Wikipedia passages (shared with SQuAD 1.1) are ubiquitous in LLM pretraining corpora
notes: Same architecture trained on SQuAD 1.1 got 85.8 F1 there (5.4 below human) vs 66.3 on SQuAD 2.0 (23.2 below human) per paper.

canonical_name: OpenBookQA ('Can a Suit of Armor Conduct Electricity? A New Dataset for Open Book Question Answering')
metric: accuracy
n_items_test: 500 (test); dev 500; train 4,957 (total 5,957). Accompanied by an 'open book' of 1,326 core science facts and ~6,000 crowdsourced auxiliary facts
n_items_source: arXiv 1809.02789v1 Table 1
score_at_release_system: Odd-one-out Solver and Question Match (tied; authors' simple neural baselines)
score_at_release_setting: Test accuracy, mean over runs (Odd-one-out 50.2 +/- 1.6; Question Match 50.2 +/- 0.9); no gold facts given. Oracle settings with gold facts: f only 55.8, f+WordNet 56.3, f+ConceptNet 53.7, f+k 76.9. Random 25.0
n_annotators: 5 crowdworkers per question (MTurk, North America, Masters qualification); the same validation answers used to keep questions (>=4/5 correct required) were used to estimate human accuracy
human_source: arXiv 1809.02789v1 Table 4 (test 91.7, dev 89.3; 'close to 92%'); estimate of expected accuracy of a random worker from a pool, with Hoeffding bound (>= estimate - 3% w.p. > 98.8%)
test_access_notes: Test questions with answer keys distributed in the public release (http://data.allenai.org/OpenBookQA); AI2 hosted a leaderboard, but labels are not withheld
curation_notes: MTurk workers shown a core science fact (subset of WorldTree corpus) composed it with a second common-knowledge fact into a 4-way MC question; filtered automatically against IR and word-association solvers and by 5-worker validation
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI (Mihaylov [Heidelberg Univ.], Clark, Khot, Sabharwal)
official_leaderboard: yes - AI2 leaderboard https://leaderboard.allenai.org/open_book_qa/submissions/public (not mentioned in paper v1; site no longer reachable)
lineage: Facts drawn from WorldTree (Jansen et al. 2018); sibling of ARC (AI2 Aristo, 2018-03); no official successor
known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed. Test set and answers public since 2018
notes: Human estimate is likely optimistic because questions were retained only if >=4 of 5 validators answered correctly and those same answers were reused.

canonical_name: DROP: Discrete Reasoning Over Paragraphs
metric: F1 (numeracy-aware token F1: F1 = 0 if numbers mismatch) and Exact Match; F1 headline
n_items_test: 9,622 questions (hidden test; 588 passages). De-facto standard for LLM reports is the public dev set: 9,536 questions (582 passages). Train 77,409 (5,565 passages); total 96,567
n_items_source: arXiv 1903.00161v1 Table 2
score_at_release_system: Augmented QANet (renamed NAQANet in v2) - authors' QANet with numerical reasoning heads
score_at_release_setting: Hidden test F1 47.01 / EM 44.07 (dev 49.24 / 46.20). Other baselines (test F1): BERT 32.70, QANet+ELMo 29.67, QANet 28.36, BiDAF 27.49
n_annotators: Paper authors collectively answered 420 test questions (v1); v2 re-estimate used 560 test questions
human_source: arXiv 1903.00161v1 Table 4 (test F1 95.98 / EM 92.38). arXiv v2 (NAACL 2019) revised to F1 96.42 / EM 94.09 on 560 test questions (value shown on leaderboard)
test_access_notes: Leaderboard with a hidden test set (paper: https://allennlp.org/drop; AI2 leaderboard); train/dev public
curation_notes: MTurk workers wrote questions over Wikipedia passages (many NFL game summaries and history articles) adversarially: questions had to defeat a live BiDAF model; answers are numbers, dates or (multiple) spans
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI / AllenNLP with UC Irvine and Peking Univ. (Dua, Wang, Dasigi, Stanovsky, Singh, Gardner)
lineage: No direct parent; companion AllenNLP reading-comprehension sets (Quoref, ROPES, 2019); DROP contrast sets in Gardner et al. 2020 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02709)
known_contamination_or_defects: Official-style scoring is brittle for generative LLMs: Hugging Face found float answers never matched due to stop-token/normalization issues and removed DROP from the Open LLM Leaderboard (2023-12-01, https://huggingface.co/blog/open-llm-leaderboard-drop). Wikipedia passages are common in pretraining data
notes: Human estimate changed between arXiv v1 (95.98 F1) and v2 (96.42 F1).

canonical_name: Social IQa: Commonsense Reasoning about Social Interactions
metric: accuracy
n_items_test: 2,224 (official hidden test, final EMNLP-2019 release); dev 1,954 (public, de-facto for LLM reports); train 33,410. arXiv v1 (2019-04) described an earlier, unfiltered version: train 33,871 / dev 5,369 / test 5,571 (44,811 total)
n_items_source: EMNLP 2019 paper (https://aclanthology.org/D19-1454) Table 1 and arXiv v2; arXiv 1904.09728v1 statistics table
score_at_release_system: BERT-large (fine-tuned)
score_at_release_setting: Final official test set (dev 66.0). arXiv v1 reported BERT-large 77.0 test (dev 77.2) on the pre-filtering v1 test set (5,571); dev/test were later reduced by lightweight adversarial filtering with a stylistic classifier. Random 33.3
score_at_release_source: https://aclanthology.org/D19-1454 Table 2 and arXiv 1904.09728v2; v1 value from arXiv 1904.09728v1 results table
n_annotators: 3 new MTurk workers per example, majority vote, on random 900 dev and 900 test examples (final version)
human_source: EMNLP 2019 Table 2 (test 84.4, dev 86.9). arXiv v2: 86.0 test / 88.1 dev on 400 sampled examples. arXiv v1: 'Human 100' by design (validation majority vote defines gold; ~90% agreement) - degenerate
test_access_notes: Public release contains only train and dev; test scored via AI2 leaderboard (https://leaderboard.allenai.org/socialiqa)
curation_notes: MTurk workers wrote contexts/questions seeded from ATOMIC event-inference dimensions; correct answers and handwritten incorrect answers plus 'Question-Switching Answers'; incorrect answers chosen least-entailed by the correct one; final dev/test adversarially filtered
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI + University of Washington (Sap, Rashkin, Chen, Le Bras, Choi)
lineage: Parent: ATOMIC knowledge graph (Sap et al. 2019); no official successor
known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed
notes: Version caveat: arXiv v1 numbers (77.0 model, 100 human, 5,571 test) are for a superseded dataset version; main fields use the final official release (same creators, 2019). Human estimate also differs between v2 (86.0) and final (84.4).

canonical_name: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems
metric: SuperGLUE score = unweighted average over 8 tasks (multi-metric tasks averaged first: CB acc/F1, MultiRC F1a/EM, ReCoRD F1/EM; accuracy otherwise)
n_items_test: ~17.6k test examples over 8 tasks (BoolQ 3,245; CB 250; COPA 500; MultiRC 1,800; ReCoRD ~10k; RTE 300; WiC 1,400; WSC 146) plus diagnostics AX-b and AX-g. arXiv v1 (2019-05) had only 6 tasks (CB, COPA, MultiRC, RTE, WiC, WSC; 4,396 test examples)
n_items_source: arXiv 1905.00537v2 task table; v1 Table 1
score_at_release_system: BERT++ (BERT-large with intermediate training on related tasks, e.g., MNLI)
score_at_release_setting: Final 8-task benchmark, test via leaderboard (BERT 69.0). arXiv v1 (6 tasks): BERT++ 69.7, BERT 66.6
n_annotators: 5 MTurk workers per example, majority vote; 100 random test examples per task (full 146-example test for WSC); training on up to 30 dev examples; $23.75/hr
human_source: arXiv 1905.00537v2 (89.8 over 8 tasks); v1 reported 89.6 over 6 tasks
test_access_notes: Private test labels; leaderboard submissions limited to 2/day and 6/month
curation_notes: Aggregates existing datasets (BoolQ, CB, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, WSC) selected via an open call for difficult tasks; diagnostics reuse GLUE diagnostic (AX-b) and Winogender (AX-g)
maintainer: NYU (Wang, Pruksachatkun, Nangia, Bowman) with Facebook AI Research, Univ. of Washington, DeepMind
lineage: Successor to GLUE (2018-04); task set grew from 6 tasks (arXiv v1, 2019-05) to 8 (arXiv v2, 2019, adding BoolQ and ReCoRD); clones include Russian SuperGLUE (2020-10)
known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed; constituent tasks (e.g., RTE, WSC, COPA) predate the benchmark and are widely circulated online
notes: Version caveat: main fields use the final 8-task version that the leaderboard uses; v1 values given in setting/source. Format = classification, MC QA, cloze-style QA mix.

canonical_name: HellaSwag ('HellaSwag: Can a Machine Really Finish Your Sentence?')
metric: accuracy (4-way multiple choice)
n_items_test: 10,003 (test, labels withheld); validation 10,042 is the de-facto standard for LLM reports; train 39,905. Paper: ~10K val / ~10K test, each half in-domain and half zero-shot; 70k contexts total (25k ActivityNet, 45k WikiHow)
n_items_source: arXiv 1905.07830v1 Table 1 / Section 4 (approximate sizes); exact counts from released files via Hugging Face datasets-server (Rowan/hellaswag)
score_at_release_system: BERT-Large (fine-tuned)
score_at_release_setting: Overall test accuracy (val 46.7); in-domain 49.7, zero-shot 45.0, ActivityNet 51.7, WikiHow 45.0. Next: OpenAI GPT 41.7, BERT-Base 40.5; chance 25.0
n_annotators: 5 independent crowdworkers per question, majority vote
human_source: arXiv 1905.07830v1 Table 1 (test 95.6, val 95.7; ActivityNet 94.0, WikiHow 96.5)
test_access_notes: Released test file is unlabeled; test scores via leaderboard (rowanzellers.com/hellaswag / AI2 leaderboard)
curation_notes: Contexts mined from ActivityNet Captions and WikiHow; wrong endings machine-generated by fine-tuned OpenAI GPT and selected via Adversarial Filtering with BERT-Large discriminators; crowdworkers validated/filtered endings
maintainer: University of Washington + Allen Institute for AI (Zellers, Holtzman, Bisk, Farhadi, Choi)
lineage: Successor to SWAG (Zellers et al. 2018-08); later GoldenSwag cleaned subset (2025), HellaSwag-Pro (2025)
known_contamination_or_defects: Chizhov et al. 2025 'What the HellaSwag?' (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07825): ~40% of validation prompts ungrammatical, 21.1% have multiple equally correct endings, 4.1% only implausible options; >65% of model predictions unchanged when the context is removed; released GoldenSwag (1,525 of 10,042 val items)
notes: Test labels hidden, so LLM papers almost universally report the validation set.

canonical_name: WinoGrande: An Adversarial Winograd Schema Challenge at Scale
metric: accuracy (2-way fill-in-the-blank); leaderboard also uses AUC over training-set sizes (XS-XL)
n_items_test: 1,767 (official hidden test, final release); dev 1,267 (de-facto for LLM reports); train XL 40,398 (sizes XS 160 / S 640 / M 2,558 / L 10,234 / XL). arXiv v1 (2019-07): 43,985 total; 'debiased' 25,680 split 18,538 / 2,863 / 4,279
n_items_source: arXiv 1907.10641v2 (AAAI 2020) tables; split counts from Hugging Face datasets-server (allenai/winogrande); v1 counts from arXiv 1907.10641v1
score_at_release_system: RoBERTa-large fine-tuned on WinoGrande XL
score_at_release_setting: Final official test (dev 79.3); range 59.4-79.1 across training sizes. arXiv v1 (pre-RoBERTa, different debiased split): best BERT-seqft 61.6 test (dev 63.5)
score_at_release_source: arXiv 1907.10641v2 abstract and results table; v1 abstract and results table
n_annotators: Majority vote of 3 crowdworkers per question
human_source: arXiv 1907.10641v2 (test 94.0, dev 94.1); arXiv v1 reported 90.8 test / 92.0 dev on the earlier split
test_access_notes: Test labels withheld; scored via AI2 leaderboard (https://leaderboard.allenai.org/winogrande); dataset at http://winogrande.allenai.org
curation_notes: MTurk workers wrote twin sentences (15-30 words, >=70% overlap) primed by WikiHow topics; validated by 3 workers; AFLITE adversarial filtering on precomputed RoBERTa/BERT embeddings removed artifact-laden items
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI + University of Washington (Sakaguchi, Le Bras, Bhagavatula, Choi)
lineage: Parent: Winograd Schema Challenge (Levesque et al. 2011; WSC273) and related WSC variants (DPR, SuperGLUE-WSC); no official successor
known_contamination_or_defects: Elazar et al. 2021 (EMNLP, https://aclanthology.org/2021.emnlp-main.819/) report artifacts in Winograd-schema benchmarks incl. WinoGrande and near-random zero-shot LM performance under stricter twin-sentence evaluation
notes: Version caveat: arXiv v1 (2019-07) used a different debiased split and predates RoBERTa; main fields use the final release (later arXiv version / AAAI 2020) that defines the official test set and leaderboard.

canonical_name: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language (Physical Interaction QA)
metric: accuracy (2-way choice between solutions)
n_items_test: 3,084 (test, labels withheld); dev 1,838 (de-facto for LLM reports); train 16,113. Paper: 'over 16,000 training ... ~2K and ~3k held out for development and testing'
n_items_source: arXiv 1911.11641v1 Section 3; exact counts from official data files (ybisk.github.io/piqa/data: train.jsonl, valid.jsonl, tests.jsonl)
score_at_release_system: RoBERTa-large (355M), fine-tuned
score_at_release_setting: Test accuracy (val 79.2). OpenAI GPT 69.2, BERT-large 66.8; majority 50.4; random 50.0
n_annotators: Majority vote of qualified annotators (>=90% on a qualification HIT); number per item not stated; evaluated on the development set
human_source: arXiv 1911.11641v1 results table (validation 94.9; no test value)
test_access_notes: Test file released without labels; predictions submitted to leaderboard (yonatanbisk.com/piqa / AI2). A separate DARPA MCS blind test (3,446 items) also existed
curation_notes: Annotators, inspired by instructables.com, wrote a goal plus a correct and a minimally different incorrect solution (non-prototypical uses of everyday objects); cleaned with AFLite adversarial filtering
maintainer: Allen Institute for AI, Univ. of Washington, Microsoft Research AI, CMU (Bisk, Zellers, Le Bras, Gao, Choi)
official_leaderboard: yes - AI2 leaderboard (leaderboard.allenai.org/physicaliqa) linked from https://yonatanbisk.com/piqa (AI2 site no longer reachable)
lineage: No direct parent; part of AI2/UW commonsense suite (SWAG, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, SIQA); no official successor
known_contamination_or_defects: GPT-3 paper flagged PIQA for potential data contamination (https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165); paper notes some dev 'mistakes' were actually correct but required web search
notes: Human baseline reported only on dev, not test.

canonical_name: Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC; now ARC-AGI-1), introduced in 'On the Measure of Intelligence'
metric: task accuracy: a task counts as solved only if the exact output grid(s) are produced for all test inputs; 3 trials per test input at release (ARC Prize 2024+ uses 2 attempts)
n_items_test: 100 private evaluation tasks (hidden; used for Kaggle 2020 and ARC Prize). Public sets: 400 training + 400 public evaluation tasks (public eval is the de-facto set for papers); 100 semi-private tasks added for ARC Prize API testing
n_items_source: github.com/fchollet/ARC README; ARC Prize 2024 Technical Report (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04604); ARC-AGI-2 paper (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11831): 'original public dataset contained 400 training tasks and 400 evaluation tasks. A Private Evaluation set of 100 tasks was reserved for competition leaderboards'
score_at_release_setting: No AI baseline reported at release. First competition (Kaggle Abstraction and Reasoning Challenge, 2020): top score ~20% on private set; no deep-learning approach above 1% (ARC Prize 2024 Technical Report)
n_annotators: 2 human testers on the original private evaluation tasks: 97% and 98% individually; 100% of tasks solved by at least one of them (union)
human_source: ARC Prize 2024 Technical Report (creators, https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04604) and ARC-AGI-2 paper. Independent H-ARC study (LeGris et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01374): 1,729 MTurk participants, avg 64.2% on public eval and 76.2% on training; 790/800 tasks solved by >=1 person in 3 attempts
test_access_notes: Training and public evaluation tasks (with answers) on GitHub; private evaluation set kept by maintainers and only scored via competitions (Kaggle 2020, ARCathon, ARC Prize); same 100 private tasks reused 2020-2024
curation_notes: Tasks hand-designed by Francois Chollet; grid puzzles (1x1 to 30x30, 10 colors) with ~3 demonstration pairs and usually 1 test input, requiring only 'core knowledge' priors
maintainer: Francois Chollet (released 2019 while at Google, personal GitHub repo); since 2024 ARC Prize Foundation (nonprofit)
official_leaderboard: no leaderboard at release; later Kaggle 2020 competition and https://arcprize.org/leaderboard
lineage: Successors: ARC-AGI-2 (2025-03), ARC-AGI-3 (interactive games; preview 2025). Derivatives: ConceptARC, RE-ARC, H-ARC human dataset
known_contamination_or_defects: ~49% of private-eval tasks solved by at least one 2020 Kaggle team, showing susceptibility to brute-force program search; public eval easier than private eval (inconsistent difficulty); same 100 private tasks reused across 2020-2024 competitions (leakage risk) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04604, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.11831). Public training/eval tasks on GitHub since 2019
notes: Paper v1 Part III could not be read in full (fetch truncated); dataset structure and human figures taken from the official repo and creator-authored ARC Prize reports. Modality: visual grids, typically fed to LLMs as JSON integer matrices.

canonical_name: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images (Task 1, single-page DocVQA)
metric: ANLS (Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity, primary) and exact-match accuracy
n_items_test: 5,188 questions on 1,287 document images (test, answers withheld); val 5,349 questions / 1,286 images; train 39,463 / 10,194 (50,000 questions on 12,767 images total)
n_items_source: arXiv 2007.00398v1 dataset statistics; DocVQA Challenge 2020 report (arXiv 2008.08899)
score_at_release_system: PingAn-OneConnect-Gammalab-DQA (external; winner of DocVQA CVPR 2020 challenge, Task 1)
score_at_release_setting: Test ANLS on RRC leaderboard; the challenge ran Mar-May 2020, before paper v1 (2020-07), so the official leaderboard already had external entries. Creators' best baseline in paper v1: BERT-large fine-tuned on SQuAD 1.1 + DocVQA, test ANLS 0.665 / accuracy 55.77% (val 0.655 / 54.48%)
n_annotators: 4 volunteers from the authors' institution answered all test questions (ANLS 0.981, accuracy 94.36%)
test_access_notes: Test answers withheld; evaluation by submission to the Robust Reading Competition portal (https://rrc.cvc.uab.es/?ch=17), open for continuous submission
curation_notes: Document images from the UCSF Industry Documents Library (6,071 documents, tobacco/food/drug/fossil fuel/chemical industries, 1900-2018); questions and answers written by remote crowdworkers in a 3-stage process (QA creation, verification, editorial review); multiple gold answers allowed
maintainer: CVC Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona + CVIT IIIT Hyderabad (Mathew, Karatzas, Jawahar; Manmatha at Amazon)
lineage: Part of the DocVQA challenge series: Task 1 single-page DocVQA (2020); later Document Collection VQA (2021), InfographicVQA (2021), MP-DocVQA (2022)
known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed; ANLS gives partial credit for near-miss strings
notes: Score_at_release uses the leaderboard top at paper release (0.85, reported to 2 decimals) per the 'external entries at launch' rule; creators' own paper baseline was 0.665. Answers are extractive from document text, judged by ANLS (format closest to short-answer with fuzzy matching).

canonical_name: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding ('the Hendrycks test')
metric: accuracy (4-way multiple choice), macro-averaged as reported (average over subjects/categories)
n_items_test: 14,042 (test in released data); validation 1,531; few-shot dev 285 (5 per subject x 57). Paper text: v1 says 15,908 total with 1,543 val / 14,080 test; v3 says 1,540 val / 14,079 test
n_items_source: arXiv 2009.03300v1 Section 3; arXiv v3; released data counts via Hugging Face datasets-server (cais/mmlu, 'all' config)
score_at_release_system: GPT-3 175B ('X-Large')
score_at_release_setting: Few-shot (5 demonstrations per subject), no fine-tuning; UnifiedQA 38.5 in v1. Later version (v3/ICLR 2021) reports UnifiedQA (T5-11B) 48.9 as best; GitHub leaderboard later adds GPT-3 fine-tuned 53.9
n_annotators: Not a direct measurement: estimated from 95th-percentile human test-taker accuracy on the source exams, with educated guesses where unavailable; separately, unspecialized MTurk humans scored 34.5%
human_source: Not in arXiv v1; added in later versions (v3 / ICLR 2021): 'expert-level accuracy is approximately 89.8%' and 'Unspecialized humans from Amazon Mechanical Turk obtain 34.5% accuracy'
test_access_notes: Full test set with answers downloadable (people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~hendrycks/data.tar)
curation_notes: Questions manually collected by graduate and undergraduate students from freely available online sources, e.g., practice questions for GRE, USMLE, AP and other exams; 57 subjects
maintainer: UC Berkeley (Hendrycks, Burns, Basart, Zou, Mazeika, Song, Steinhardt)
official_leaderboard: informal - GitHub README 'Test Leaderboard' (https://github.com/hendrycks/test), updated via pull requests
lineage: Draws partly on ETHICS (2020) for moral scenarios; successors/variants: CMMLU (2023-06), MMLU-Pro (2024-06), MMLU-Redux (2024-06), OpenAI MMMLU multilingual (2024-09), Global-MMLU (2024-12)
known_contamination_or_defects: MMLU-Redux (Gema et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04127): ~6.49% of questions contain errors; 57% of analysed Virology questions erroneous. Test set public since 2020 and widely circulated online (contamination risk)
notes: Human baselines were not in v1; values from the later version of the same paper.

canonical_name: RussianSuperGLUE: A Russian Language Understanding Evaluation Benchmark
metric: overall score = average over 9 tasks of task metrics (MCC for LiDiRus; F1/acc for RCB; F1/EM for MuSeRC and RuCoS; accuracy otherwise), reported on 0-1 scale
n_items_test: ~22.1k test items over 9 tasks (v1 table: LiDiRus 1,104 diagnostic; RUSSE 12,151; PARus 400; TERRa 3,198; RCB 348; RWSD 154; MuSeRC 322; RuCoS 4,147; DaNetQA 295)
n_items_source: arXiv 2010.15925v1 task table (sum computed)
score_at_release_system: RuBERT (DeepPavlov), fine-tuned per task (authors' baseline)
score_at_release_setting: Test via leaderboard; Multilingual BERT 0.542, TF-IDF 0.461. Paper v1 reports only authors' baselines (no external leaderboard entries listed)
n_annotators: 3-5 Yandex.Toloka crowdworkers per example, majority vote; full test sets annotated except RUSSE (5,000 sampled) and RuCoS (1,000 sampled)
human_source: arXiv 2010.15925v1 Table 2 (0.802). Leaderboard later listed human 0.811 (per Iazykova et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.01192); v1.1 (2022) re-collected human scores for RUSSE and DaNetQA
test_access_notes: Test sets distributed without answers; scoring via submission on https://russiansuperglue.com
curation_notes: Nine tasks following SuperGLUE design: translated & professionally edited (LiDiRus from GLUE diagnostic, PARus from COPA, RWSD from Winograd Schema Challenge); mined & rule-filtered from Taiga web corpus with manual post-processing (TERRa, RCB); crowdsourced on Toloka (MuSeRC questions/answers, DaNetQA yes/no questions); converted existing resources (RUSSE WSD -> WiC format); auto-generated cloze queries from Lenta/Deutsche Welle news (RuCoS)
maintainer: Sberbank/SberDevices AI with HSE University, MIPT, Huawei Noah's Ark Lab (Shavrina, Fenogenova et al.); now RussianNLP
official_leaderboard: yes - https://russiansuperglue.com/leaderboard (site not reachable during this check)
lineage: Modeled on SuperGLUE (2019); Russian SuperGLUE 1.1 (2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.07791) expanded/cleaned RUSSE, DaNetQA, RuCoS, MuSeRC; later Russian LLM benchmark MERA (2024)
known_contamination_or_defects: v1.1 paper reports data leakage (e.g., RUSSE: mBART ~99% vs human 75%), unbalanced test class distributions, typos/inconsistencies (https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.07791); simple rule-based heuristics scored 0.468, matching ruGPT3-Medium (Iazykova et al. 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.01192)
notes: Leaderboard snapshot dates and launch-time entries could not be verified (site unreachable). Format: classification, MC, and reading-comprehension (F1/EM) mix.

canonical_name: MATH: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset (Hendrycks et al.); MATH-500 subset from 'Let's Verify Step by Step'
metric: accuracy (exact match of final \boxed{} answer after normalization)
n_items_test: 5,000 (test); train 7,500 (12,500 total; 7 subjects, difficulty levels 1-5). MATH-500: 500 test problems selected uniformly at random by Lightman et al. (OpenAI, 2023-05), now a de-facto standard subset
n_items_source: arXiv 2103.03874v1 abstract/Section 3; MATH-500: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.20050
score_at_release_system: GPT-2 1.5B pretrained on AMPS then fine-tuned on MATH train
score_at_release_setting: Direct final-answer generation (no CoT); GPT-3 175B 8-shot few-shot 5.2; GPT-3 2.7B 2.9; GPT-2 0.1B 5.4. MATH-500 at its introduction (2023-05): 78.2% (GPT-4-based PRM, best-of-1860)
n_annotators: 6 university students on 20 randomly sampled test problems (1 hour, by hand): 40% (dislikes math), 65%, 70%, 75%, 90% (AMC10 perfect/USAMO), 90% (three-time IMO gold medalist)
human_source: arXiv 2103.03874v1 Section on human-level performance
test_access_notes: Full test problems and solutions released (GitHub hendrycks/math)
curation_notes: Competition problems (AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, and more) collected from AoPS with full step-by-step LaTeX solutions; accompanied by AMPS pretraining corpus (Khan Academy + ~5M Mathematica-generated problems, 23 GB)
maintainer: UC Berkeley (Hendrycks, Burns, Kadavath, Arora, Basart, Tang, Song, Steinhardt)
lineage: Related prior work: DeepMind Mathematics Dataset (2019). Subsets/variants: MATH-500 (Lightman et al., 2023-05), Functional MATH() (2024-02), MATH-Perturb (2025); companion AMPS pretraining corpus
known_contamination_or_defects: Problems and solutions are on AoPS and public since 2021 (contamination risk); functional variant MATH() shows 58-80% 'reasoning gap' vs static accuracy for SOTA models (Srivastava et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.19450); 4,500 of the 5,000 test problems were used as training data in PRM800K (Lightman et al. 2023), motivating MATH-500
notes: Human figures are tiny-sample (n=20 problems).

canonical_name: HumanEval (introduced in 'Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code', Codex paper)
metric: pass@k via unbiased estimator (n=200 samples); pass@1 is the standard headline
n_items_test: 164 problems (avg 7.7 unit tests each); no train/dev split
n_items_source: arXiv 2107.03374v1 Section 2
score_at_release_system: Codex-S-12B (Codex further fine-tuned on correctly implemented standalone functions)
score_at_release_setting: pass@1, single sample. Codex-12B: pass@1 28.81 / pass@10 46.81 / pass@100 72.31 (abstract: 28.8%, 70.2% with 100 samples); Codex-S pass@100 77.5; Codex-S + mean-log-p reranking of 100 samples 44.5; GPT-J 6B 11.62; GPT-3 ~0
human_source: No human baseline in paper
test_access_notes: Problems, canonical solutions and tests released at https://github.com/openai/human-eval
curation_notes: 164 hand-written Python programming problems (signature, docstring, body, unit tests) written by OpenAI researchers to avoid GitHub contamination; language comprehension, algorithms, simple math
maintainer: OpenAI
lineage: Variants/extensions: HumanEval+ / EvalPlus (2023-05, 80x tests), multilingual translations MultiPL-E (2022) and HumanEval-X (2023); widely paired with MBPP (Google, 2021-08)
known_contamination_or_defects: Insufficient tests: EvalPlus extends tests 80x (HumanEval+) and pass@k drops by up to 19.3-28.9% (Liu et al. 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.01210). Problems public on GitHub since 2021 (contamination risk)

canonical_name: GSM8K: Grade School Math 8K (introduced in 'Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems')
metric: accuracy / test solve rate (exact match of final numeric answer after '####')
n_items_test: 1,319 (test); train 7,473 (paper: '7.5K training problems and 1K test problems')
n_items_source: Counted from official files github.com/openai/grade-school-math (test.jsonl, train.jsonl); arXiv 2110.14168v1
score_at_release_system: GPT-3 175B fine-tuned generator + trained verifier (best-of-100 samples ranked by verifier), with calculator annotations
score_at_release_setting: Computed from creators' released per-problem test solutions (742/1,319 marked correct): 175B verification 56.25, 175B fine-tuning 34.72, 6B verification 39.04, 6B fine-tuning 21.68. Paper reports these only in figures; launch blog: 'our system scored 55%' on the problems given to children
n_annotators: 'a small sample of 9-12 year olds' (size not stated) on a test drawn from the dataset
human_source: OpenAI launch blog post 2021-10-29 (not in paper v1)
test_access_notes: Test questions and worked solutions released on GitHub
curation_notes: Problems written by paid human problem writers (contractors via Upwork and Surge AI) with natural-language solutions; quality control by worker answer agreement; authors estimate <2% of problems contain breaking errors (1.7% residual disagreement)
maintainer: OpenAI (Cobbe et al.)
lineage: Successors/variants: GSM-Hard (PAL, 2022-11), GSM1k (Scale AI, 2024-05), GSM-Symbolic (Apple, 2024-10), GSM8K-Platinum (MIT Madry lab, 2025; cleaned test set); Socratic-subquestion variant released with the dataset
known_contamination_or_defects: GSM1k: accuracy drops up to 8% vs GSM8K, correlated with models' likelihood of generating GSM8K items (Zhang et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00332); GSM8K-Platinum removed 110 flawed test questions and relabeled 10 (1,209 remain) (https://huggingface.co/datasets/madrylab/gsm8k-platinum, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03461)
notes: Score_at_release is a count from creator-released outputs, not a number printed in the paper text.

canonical_name: BIG-Bench Hard (BBH), from 'Challenging BIG-Bench Tasks and Whether Chain-of-Thought Can Solve Them'
metric: exact-match accuracy, averaged over the 23 tasks
n_items_test: 6,511 examples across 23 tasks / 27 subtask files (max 250 examples per task, 3 exceptions); no train split (3 few-shot CoT exemplars per task provided)
n_items_source: arXiv 2210.09261v1; total confirmed by counting the 27 files in github.com/suzgunmirac/BIG-Bench-Hard/bbh
score_at_release_system: Codex (code-davinci-002)
score_at_release_setting: 3-shot chain-of-thought prompting, average over 23 tasks (Codex answer-only 3-shot: 56.6). InstructGPT text-davinci-002 CoT 68.4 (answer-only 51.8); PaLM 540B CoT 65.2 (answer-only 52.3). Best prior BIG-Bench result on these tasks: 50.9
n_annotators: BIG-Bench human raters (from Srivastava et al. 2022); also max human-rater average 94.4
human_source: arXiv 2210.09261v1 (average human-rater 67.7; max human-rater 94.4), originally collected for BIG-Bench (https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04615)
test_access_notes: All examples, prompts and Codex outputs released on GitHub; BIG-Bench canary string convention
curation_notes: Subset of community-contributed BIG-Bench tasks (mix of expert-written, templated/synthetic and adapted items). Filtering 209 -> 23: <=3 subtasks (187), >=103 examples (130), human-rater baseline available (85), multiple-choice/exact-match metric (78), no prior model above average human-rater (36), then manual exclusion of out-of-scope tasks (23)
maintainer: Google Research/Brain + Stanford (Suzgun, Scales, Scharli, Gehrmann, Tay, Chung, Chowdhery, Le, Chi, Zhou, Wei)
lineage: Parent: BIG-Bench (2022-06, https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04615); successor: BIG-Bench Extra Hard (BBEH, Google DeepMind, 2025-02, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.19187), which replaces each BBH task citing saturation
known_contamination_or_defects: BBEH authors state SOTA models reach near-perfect scores on many BBH tasks (saturation). No specific label-error audit found in sources reviewed
notes: At release the best creator-reported model (73.9) already exceeded the average human-rater (67.7); Codex+CoT beat average human-rater on 17/23 tasks. Mix of MC-style and free-form exact-match answers.

canonical_name: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
metric: end-to-end task success rate (functional-correctness evaluators: string match incl. LLM fuzzy match, URL match, programmatic state checks)
n_items_test: 812 tasks instantiated from 241 intent templates (paper); ~4% unachievable ('N/A'). Current config file: 812 tasks (36 with 'N/A' references)
n_items_source: arXiv 2307.13854v1 Section 3; counted from github.com/web-arena-x/webarena config_files/test.raw.json
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 agent with reasoning-before-acting (CoT) prompting
score_at_release_setting: Text observation (accessibility tree), few-shot prompted agent; GPT-3.5 direct 7.14, GPT-3.5 reasoning 7.38. After annotation fixes (v0.2.0, 2023-10) later paper versions report GPT-4 CoT 14.41 without unachievable-hint (11.70 with hint)
score_at_release_source: arXiv 2307.13854v1 Table 3; later arXiv v4 main results table
n_annotators: 5 computer-science graduate students; one task sampled from each of 170 templates
human_source: Not in arXiv v1; added in later versions (v4/ICLR 2024): human success 78.24% (info-seeking 74.68%, others 81.32%)
test_access_notes: Task intents, reference answers and evaluator configs public on GitHub; environment self-hosted via Docker/AMI
curation_notes: Task intents written by the authors following annotation guidelines, as templates instantiated with variables; reference answers curated by authors and an external annotator (each annotated twice, third annotator resolves disagreements); sites are self-hosted open-source apps populated with real-world-like data
maintainer: Carnegie Mellon University (Zhou, Xu, Zhu, Zhou, Lo, Sridhar, Cheng, Ou, Bisk, Fried, Alon, Neubig)
official_leaderboard: yes - Google Sheets leaderboard linked from https://github.com/web-arena-x/webarena (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1M801lEpBbKSNwP-vDBkC_pF7LdyGU1f_ufZb_NWNBZQ)
lineage: Successors/variants: VisualWebArena (2024-01), WebArena-Lite subset (VisualAgentBench, 2024-08), WebArena-Verified (ServiceNow, 2025; all 812 tasks audited, 258-task Hard subset), TheAgentCompany (2024-12); integrated into BrowserGym/AgentLab
known_contamination_or_defects: Creators re-examined the dataset and fixed annotation bugs in v0.2.0 (2023-10-24, GitHub README). ServiceNow's WebArena-Verified manually reviewed and corrected every task, reference answer and evaluator, removing LLM-judge and substring matching (https://github.com/ServiceNow/webarena-verified)
notes: Websites: OneStopShop e-commerce, shopping admin CMS, Postmill (Reddit-like), GitLab, OpenStreetMap, plus Wikipedia and tools. Paper reports 241 templates; the current config lists 190 distinct intent_template_id values (possible ID merging; not resolved).

canonical_name: LegalBench: A Collaboratively Built Benchmark for Measuring Legal Reasoning in Large Language Models
metric: per-task exact-match accuracy / balanced accuracy (classification), F1 (extraction), manual grading for rule-application (correctness and analysis); reported as averages per reasoning category
n_items_test: ~90.2k test samples over 162 tasks (paper: >=50 samples per task, mean 563); Hugging Face release: 90,205 test + 1,545 train (few-shot) rows across 161 task configs (91,750 total)
n_items_source: arXiv 2308.11462v1; Hugging Face datasets-server for nguha/legalbench
score_at_release_system: GPT-4 (best of 20 LLMs from 11 families)
score_at_release_setting: Few-shot prompting (0-8 in-context demonstrations from train split). No overall score reported. GPT-4 category averages: issue-spotting 82.9, rule-recall 59.2, rule-conclusion 89.9, interpretation 75.2, rhetorical-understanding 79.4; rule-application correctness 82.2 / analysis 79.7 (manually graded). Unweighted mean of the 5 automated category averages = 77.3 (computed here, not reported)
human_source: No human or lawyer baseline reported in paper
test_access_notes: Tasks and labels public on GitHub/Hugging Face (task licenses vary; one of 162 tasks not in the HF release)
curation_notes: Crowdsourced from ~40 legal-professional contributors (lawyers, law professors, computational legal researchers): hand-crafted new tasks, previously unpublished datasets, and restructured existing legal NLP datasets (36 data sources)
maintainer: Stanford HazyResearch (Guha et al.) with contributing legal scholars and practitioners
official_leaderboard: no official leaderboard (project page https://hazyresearch.stanford.edu/legalbench/); third-party leaderboard by Vals.ai (https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/legal_bench)
lineage: Builds on/incorporates earlier legal NLP datasets (36 sources); described by creators as ongoing/extensible; related later benchmark LegalBench-RAG (2024)
known_contamination_or_defects: None specific found in sources reviewed; some constituent tasks derive from previously public datasets
notes: Score_at_release left empty because the paper reports only per-category averages (see setting). Format: mostly label classification; some extraction and free-text rule-application tasks.
